name: Exit Ticket
description: Two quick questions students answer as they arrive or before they leave. No waiting for the class, and the answers stay private to you.
when: When you need to know what landed before they walk out, from every student, not the four who raise a hand.

ticket: Plants make their own food from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
Where does the oxygen actually come out of the leaf?
Photosynthesis happens in the chloroplasts, and chlorophyll is what makes leaves green.
Do plants do it at night too, or only in daylight?
The outputs are glucose and oxygen. The plant keeps the sugar and lets the oxygen go.
Is the glucose the same sugar that is in candy?
Water comes up from the roots and carbon dioxide comes in through tiny holes in the leaves.
What are the tiny holes called again?
It is basically the opposite of breathing: we take in oxygen, plants take in carbon dioxide.
Why do leaves look green if chlorophyll absorbs light?
Without photosynthesis there is no food chain, because everything eats plants or eats things that ate plants.
What happens to a plant in a dark closet for a week?
The equation has to balance: six carbon dioxide and six water make one glucose and six oxygen.
Where does the energy in the sugar come from, exactly?
Plants store extra glucose as starch, which is why potatoes are starchy.
Do mushrooms do photosynthesis? They are not green.

ticket.prompt: Answer in a sentence or two.
ticket.doneMessage: Thanks, that is all we need from you. You can put your device away.

end.message: That is everyone. Thanks for the honest answers.
